signed_prior_tick_vs_e7_delay_plus_one.definition: candidate is sample 0, 1, or 2 minus Mode A; delay is authoritative E7 delay-plus-one minus Mode A. All three prior-tick stages have identical source values.

comparison.interpretation: The prior-tick body/root pose is the near-exact signed inverse of the authoritative delay-plus-one pose around Mode A, with essentially unit magnitude. This supports the earlier-pose component of the hypothesis. Both prior and Mode-A samples publish exactly zero velocity, so the proposed velocity discriminator is falsified.

conclusion.summary: The WaitingForPoseSearch trace exposed the predicted prior fixed tick. Its pose delta is almost exactly opposite E7's one-tick-later delta around Mode A, supporting the earlier-source explanation. Its velocity is exactly the same zero publication as Mode A, falsifying velocity timing as the discriminator. The trace did not replay that source through observation packing, so historical Mode B has not yet been reproduced.
conclusion.what_was_learned: The startup chronology contains a symmetric live-pose sequence centered on Mode A: the 0.0166667-second source is one nearly equal step before it, and E7's 0.0500000-second source is one step after it. Runtime-state changes within either observed tick do not alter the body source. Historical Mode B differs from Mode A in all 214 self-observation pose slots but none of the 144 all-zero velocity slots. The next uncertainty is whether the prior-tick MannyCurrentBodySamples source reconstructs the exact historical Mode-B tensor through the unchanged Manny-to-canonical adapter and observation builder.
